label: rem:bar-involution-grading-lean-proofs
title: The $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ bar-grading: Lean $\leftrightarrow$ paper proof bridge
html:
This remark is the \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} bar-grading Lean \leftrightarrow paper bridge for the bar-involution: the bar-grading subring/module structure and the sorry-free Lean theorems with their narrative proofs.

Proofs (Lean \leftrightarrow paper bridge)

Every Lean theorem in bar-involution.lean has both a narrative proof here and a sorry-free formal proof. Theorems split into three sections by structural prerequisite (CommRing / Field).

Bar-grading over CommRing R

Proposition (Lean: decompose x). x = P_{\mathrm{avg}}(x) + P_{\mathrm{skew}}(x). Proof. \frac{x + \overline x}{2} + \frac{x - \overline x}{2} = \frac{2x}{2} = x. \square

Proposition (Lean: isBarSymmetric_zero, isBarSymmetric_one). 0 and 1 are bar-symmetric. Proof. Direct from BarInvolution.bar_zero and bar_one. \square

Proposition (Lean: IsBarSymmetric.add). Sum of bar-symmetric is bar-symmetric. Proof. \overline{x+y} = \overline x + \overline y = x + y. \square

Proposition (Lean: IsBarSymmetric.mul). Product of bar-symmetric is bar-symmetric. Proof. \overline{x \cdot y} = \overline x \cdot \overline y = x \cdot y. \square

Proposition (Lean: IsBarAntiSymmetric.add). Sum of bar-anti-symmetric is bar-anti-symmetric. Proof. \overline{x+y} = \overline x + \overline y = -x + (-y) = -(x+y). \square

Theorem (Lean: IsBarSymmetric.of_mul_antisym). x, y bar-anti-symmetric \Rightarrow x \cdot y bar-symmetric. Proof. \overline{x \cdot y} = \overline x \cdot \overline y = (-x)(-y) = x \cdot y. This is the "anti \times anti = sym" identity that generates the bar-symmetric content from bar-anti-symmetric kernels (e.g., h^2 bar-sym from h bar-anti-sym). \square

Theorem (Lean: IsBarAntiSymmetric.of_sym_mul). x bar-symmetric, y bar-anti-symmetric \Rightarrow x \cdot y bar-anti-symmetric. Proof. \overline{x \cdot y} = \overline x \cdot \overline y = x \cdot (-y) = -(x \cdot y). \square

Proposition (Lean: bar_neg x). \overline{-x} = -\overline x — bar commutes with negation. Proof. From x + (-x) = 0 and bar additive: \overline x + \overline{-x} = \overline 0 = 0, hence \overline{-x} = -\overline x. \square

Proposition (Lean: IsBarSymmetric.neg, IsBarAntiSymmetric.neg). Negation preserves both grading sectors. Proof. For sym: \overline{-x} = -\overline x = -x. For anti-sym: \overline{-x} = -\overline x = -(-x) = x = -(-x). \square

Theorem (Lean: IsBarAntiSymmetric.pow_two_mul). x bar-anti-sym \Rightarrow x^{2n} bar-symmetric. Proof. Induction on n. Base (n=0): x^0 = 1 bar-symmetric. Step: x^{2(k+1)} = x^{2k} \cdot (x \cdot x); x^{2k} bar-sym by IH, x \cdot x bar-sym by of_mul_antisym; product bar-sym by IsBarSymmetric.mul. \square

Theorem (Lean: IsBarAntiSymmetric.pow_two_mul_add_one). x bar-anti-sym \Rightarrow x^{2n+1} bar-anti-symmetric. Proof. x^{2n+1} = x^{2n} \cdot x; x^{2n} bar-sym (above), x bar-anti-sym (hypothesis); product bar-anti-sym by of_sym_mul. \square

Bar on integer scalars

Proposition (Lean: bar_two). \overline 2 = 2. Proof. \overline 2 = \overline{1 + 1} = \overline 1 + \overline 1 = 1 + 1 = 2. \square

Proposition (Lean: bar_natCast n). \overline n = n for every n \in \mathbb{N}. Proof. Induction on n. Base: \overline 0 = 0. Step: \overline{k+1} = \overline k + \overline 1 = k + 1. \square

Proposition (Lean: isBarSymmetric_natCast n). Every natural-number scalar is bar-symmetric. Proof. Restatement of bar_natCast n in the IsBarSymmetric predicate. \square

Projection theorems (require Field R)

Proposition (Lean: bar_inv x). \overline{x^{-1}} = (\overline x)^{-1} over a field. Proof. If x = 0: both sides are 0 (from \overline 0 = 0 + 0^{-1} = 0 convention). If x \neq 0: \overline x \neq 0 (bar is injective by involutivity), and \overline x \cdot \overline{x^{-1}} = \overline{x \cdot x^{-1}} = \overline 1 = 1, hence \overline{x^{-1}} = (\overline x)^{-1}. \square

Proposition (Lean: bar_half). \overline{1/2} = 1/2 over a field. Proof. \overline{1/2} = \overline{1 \cdot 2^{-1}} = \overline 1 \cdot (\overline 2)^{-1} = 1 \cdot 2^{-1} = 1/2 via bar_inv and bar_two. \square

Proposition (Lean: isBarSymmetric_intCast n). Every integer scalar is bar-symmetric. Proof. For n = \mathrm{ofNat}\, k: use bar_natCast. For n = \mathrm{negSucc}\, k = -(k+1): \overline{-(k+1)} = -\overline{k+1} = -(k+1) via bar_neg + bar_natCast. \square

Proposition (Lean: barSymmetricProjection_of_sym x). If x is bar-symmetric, P_{\mathrm{avg}}(x) = x. Proof. P_{\mathrm{avg}}(x) = (x + \overline x)/2 = (x + x)/2 = x. \square

Proposition (Lean: barSymmetricProjection_of_antisym x). If x is bar-anti-symmetric, P_{\mathrm{avg}}(x) = 0. Proof. P_{\mathrm{avg}}(x) = (x + \overline x)/2 = (x - x)/2 = 0. \square

Proposition (Lean: barSkewProjection_of_antisym x). If x is bar-anti-symmetric, P_{\mathrm{skew}}(x) = x. Proof. P_{\mathrm{skew}}(x) = (x - \overline x)/2 = (x - (-x))/2 = x. \square

Proposition (Lean: barSkewProjection_of_sym x). If x is bar-symmetric, P_{\mathrm{skew}}(x) = 0. Proof. P_{\mathrm{skew}}(x) = (x - \overline x)/2 = (x - x)/2 = 0. \square

Theorem (Lean: barSymmetricProjection_pow_even_of_antisym x n). For bar-anti-sym x: P_{\mathrm{avg}}(x^{2n}) = x^{2n}. Proof. x^{2n} is bar-symmetric by pow_two_mul; apply of_sym. \square

Theorem (Lean: barSymmetricProjection_pow_odd_of_antisym x n). For bar-anti-sym x: P_{\mathrm{avg}}(x^{2n+1}) = 0. Proof. x^{2n+1} is bar-anti-sym by pow_two_mul_add_one; apply of_antisym. This is "the framework projects away odd-power components" at the formal level. \square

Theorem (Lean: barSymmetricProjection_isBarSymmetric x). P_{\mathrm{avg}}(x) is bar-symmetric for every x. Proof. \overline{P_{\mathrm{avg}}(x)} = \overline{(x + \overline x)/2} = \overline{x + \overline x} \cdot \overline{1/2} = (\overline x + x) \cdot (1/2) = P_{\mathrm{avg}}(x) via bar_half. \square

Theorem (Lean: barSymmetricProjection_idempotent x). P_{\mathrm{avg}}^2 = P_{\mathrm{avg}}. Proof. P_{\mathrm{avg}}(x) is bar-symmetric by the previous theorem; applying P_{\mathrm{avg}} to a bar-symmetric input gives the input back by of_sym. \square

Theorem (Lean: barSkewProjection_isBarAntiSymmetric x). P_{\mathrm{skew}}(x) is bar-anti-symmetric. Proof. \overline{P_{\mathrm{skew}}(x)} = \overline{(x - \overline x)/2} = (\overline x - x) \cdot (1/2) = -P_{\mathrm{skew}}(x). \square

Theorem (Lean: barSkewProjection_idempotent x). P_{\mathrm{skew}}^2 = P_{\mathrm{skew}}. Proof. Analogous to P_{\mathrm{avg}} idempotency via barSkewProjection_of_antisym. \square

All 33 theorems / definitions in bar-involution.lean have narrative proofs here and sorry-free Lean proofs.
